name: Abijah
overview: Abijah was a male Aaronic priest from the tribe of Levi, identified in the book of Nehemiah. He is noted specifically for his role as a priest and is mentioned among those who sealed a significant covenant document. His inclusion in this record highlights his standing within the priestly community during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Abijah means '[my] father is YHWH,' reflecting a theophoric element that honors God. This proper name, as recorded in Nehemiah, does not indicate that it was given directly by God but carries a clear declaration of divine parentage or protection.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Abijah was the son of Zichri, as inferred from Nehemiah 12:17. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text for Abijah.
scriptureSignificance: Abijah's significance lies in his role as an Aaronic priest participating in the covenant renewal under Nehemiah's leadership. His name appears on the sealed document in Nehemiah 10, marking him as a key religious figure committed to the spiritual reforms of Israel after the exile. This underscores his contribution to the restoration of proper worship and covenant faithfulness among the returned exiles.
